body:
When `--replace` can't find `old`, say why. When it did apply but the retry failed, say the draft now holds the change.

## Why
In run 00acbe40d2cf4d4d on task:3517183e01f63016, steps 38–92 are mostly `E0105 \`old\` does not occur; read the current text and copy it exactly`. That message gives no clue. At least one miss happened because an earlier `--replace` had already changed the draft (step 39): the replacement applied, the retry failed, and the reply said only "Nothing was saved. Draft … retained." So the worker's idea of the draft's text was wrong from then on.

## What changes
1. **E0105 names the nearest line.** When `old` doesn't occur, `drafts.replace` names the line of the text closest to `old`'s first non-blank line, with its line number. If they differ only in leading space, it also gives each one's leading spaces, as E0108 does (D-142). If, in a patch draft, `old` matches once the `-`, `+` or ` ` prefixes are left off, the refusal says to include the prefixes. This covers `submit --draft … --replace`, `write --draft … --replace` and `submit <name> --replace`, since they share `drafts.replace`.
2. **A replacement kept in a failed retry is named.** When `--replace` applied but the retry was refused, the footer (`drafts.retry_advice`) says the draft now has the replacement, and that the next `old` must match the draft as it is now (`view --draft <id>`).

## Cautions
- **Wording only.** What `--replace` accepts doesn't change. A loose match is named, never applied.
- "Nearest" is the agent's choice of a simple measure (for example, the same line with spaces trimmed first, then the longest shared start). Keep it cheap and deterministic, and say in your summary which measure you used.
- Update `drafts.tests::replace_all_and_occurrence_lines` only where its expected message changes, and say so.

## Done when
- An `old` that differs only in leading space, or only in missing patch prefixes, gets a refusal that names the line and the fix. A plain miss names the nearest line. All are pinned by tests in `drafts::`.
- A failed retry after an applied `--replace` says the draft holds it, pinned by a test.
- `src/reference.txt`'s draft paragraph mentions that a failed retry keeps the replacement, keeping the D-143 layout.
title: drafts: --replace misses name the nearest line
